definition: Two distinct names denote literally the same nonconstant property; recognition of that identity is a separate relation and may fail. Distinct names are not automatically nonsynonymous concepts, and lack of recognition is not a proof of philosophically meaningful openness. The countermodel refutes only an inference from nonrecognition to property nonidentity.
note: Stipulated semantic test prompted by the proponents’ natural-definition replies. A full open-question or normative adequacy argument needs substantive semantics and epistemology beyond these names and denotations.
